items.grounds: Re-derived both ways from bytes. The shipped rear-edge warrant is 'at the chapter's own close' — a chapter-division fact, tier-4 under campaign law, never boundary evidence — and the row names no discriminator against the next verse anywhere: boundary_evidence_refs carries no web:Isa.12.1, and the rationale's only other rear-edge support is the onset/close inclusio, which argues internal cohesion, not a seam. The tier-1 discriminator stands unengaged in the bytes: oshb:Isa.12.1 opens וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (collate: byte), a fresh second-person speech formula that the closing verse oshb:Isa.11.16 does not carry (byte read of both staged verses). The seam itself is sound — the following unit opens on exactly that formula — so the defect is the stated warrant, not the boundary: medium confirmed (defective warrant, not alone load-bearing).

Re-swept from bytes. device_notes splices אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשָּׁאֵר֩ (oshb:Isa.11.11) and לִשְׁאָ֣ר עַמּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּׁאֵ֖ר (oshb:Isa.11.16), labels both byte tier, then ships 'that verb form reaching exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses)' with no tier on the digit. The two verb forms are not byte-equal — יִשָּׁאֵר֩ against יִשָּׁאֵ֖ר, differing in their accents — and at byte tier each stands at 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, MT Isa.11.11; sweep: 1 verse, MT Isa.11.16). The 2 obtains only at accent-stripped and at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses, MT Isa.11.11 and Isa.11.16, at each of those tiers; the skeleton hits are word-bound in the staged index) — tiers the row never names, while the same field's other recurrence claim does name its tiers. Defective digit claim in a non-driving disclosure field (the boundary is argued from the agent shift): medium confirmed.

Re-derived. The row's span is Isa.13.17-Isa.13.22, so web:Isa.13.22 is its own closing verse, yet device_notes states that וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.13.22, collate: byte) 'closes the following unit's last line' — positionally false here, where the following unit is Isa.14.1-Isa.14.2. Byte-diff of the two embedded device_notes fields confirms the copy: a single maximal common block of 1,009 characters (82.2% of this row's 1,227-character field), running from 'A two-site shatter-root catchword straddles the seam' to the shared field-final 'does not outweigh.', carried unchanged from the preceding row (span Isa.13.1-Isa.13.16), where the same sentence is true. The underlying devices re-verify: כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב (oshb:Isa.13.6, collate: byte), and the shatter-root at skeleton tier at exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT Isa.13.16 and Isa.13.18). Byte-false positional claim inside a non-driving disclosure field: medium confirmed.

Re-derived. oshb:Isa.14.1 opens כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֗ב (collate: byte) — a third-person verb with object-marked Jacob — and the whole staged verse carries no second-person form, no vocative, and no imperative (byte read); the staged WEB rendering of web:Isa.14.1 is likewise third person throughout. The rationale's rear-edge look-ahead 'turns the addressee to Jacob at web:Isa.14.1' therefore misstates the signal class; the seam itself holds on the participant shift, tier-1 where explicit in the bytes under the ruled inventory, so the label is the defect, not the cut. The same mislabel recurs in the next row's own-onset warrant (ruled separately); the seam-pair cure is one edit. Defective warrant label, not alone load-bearing: medium confirmed.

Re-derived. oshb:Isa.14.1-14.2 is third person throughout at byte tier — כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֗ב and וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.14.1, collate: byte); וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ and וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם (oshb:Isa.14.2, collate: byte) — with no second-person form and no vocative, and oshb:Isa.13.22 closing the prior unit is likewise third person (byte read). Yet the row ships the signal key oracle_frame.addressee_shift_restoration_promise and calls Jacob 'a fresh addressee' while itself stating he is the object of both verbs — a verbal object is not an addressee. The first explicit second person in this stretch stands one verse later: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.14.3, collate: byte), the next row's onset, not this seam. The seam survives as a participant/topic shift plus the single-witness SAMEKH at MT 14:2 (pmarks inventory, tier-3), so the defect is the overstated warrant class and signal key: medium confirmed; the relabel travels with the prior row's rear-edge cure as one seam-pair edit.

Re-derived. The left-edge binding warrant 'runs as one sentence into' is a fact of the WEB rendering — the staged WEB verse at web:Isa.14.3 ends on a comma and web:Isa.14.4 opens as its subordinate continuation — i.e. translation sentence punctuation, tier-4 under campaign law, barred as driver or corroboration; the row splices no bytes from oshb:Isa.14.3 and boundary_evidence_refs carries only the WEB side of that verse. The byte-tier ground carrying the same continuity stands unnamed: oshb:Isa.14.3 opens וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (collate: byte) and oshb:Isa.14.4 continues with the waw-consecutive וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ (collate: byte), a protasis-apodosis chain binding the two verses under the ruled continuous-sentence rule. The boundary re-derives sound; the shipped warrant's tier is the defect: medium confirmed.

Re-derived. boundary_evidence_refs holds no oshb:Isa.14.3 and the rationale splices nothing from that verse, while device_notes and the signal key narrative_frame.direct_second_person_taunt rest the opening seam on the second-person turn there, and the row ships confidence high. The signal is real in the bytes: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔, then מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ, then verse-final אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד בָּֽךְ (all oshb:Isa.14.3, collate: byte) — second-person pronominals wholly absent from oshb:Isa.14.1-14.2 (third person throughout, byte read). As cited, the left edge rests on a tier-4 WEB sentence fact plus the single-witness SAMEKH at MT 14:2 (pmarks inventory, tier-3), with the tier-1 ground unengaged — an engagement-class defect the high confidence does not survive as written. Medium confirmed; add the splices and re-test the confidence.

Re-derived. oshb:Isa.14.28 is a single regnal dating clause ending verse-final in the demonstrative — הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה (collate: byte) — which is anaphoric-capable, and nothing else in the verse fixes direction (byte read of the whole staged verse). The rationale's 'pointing forward to the burden this row's own span carries' therefore ships as an ungrounded load-bearing construal: on the backward construal the verse closes the preceding oracle and this row opens at Isa.14.29. strongest_rejected_alternative disposes only of the form question (mid-verse reference vs the ten verse-initial headers) in its single sentence; the slot for the rival disclosure is unused and the direction rival appears nowhere in the row. The boundary is not shown wrong — the PE at MT 14:27 (pmarks inventory, single-witness tier-3) and the second-person Philistia address opening oshb:Isa.14.29 (byte read) support the forward reading — so the defect is the undisclosed rival and the ungrounded direction claim: medium confirmed.
